Subject: Realtime feed freeze — seeing 10–30s blackouts during bursts

Hi Stephanie,

We started seeing intermittent blackouts on our live inference feed this morning during a scheduled surge test. Clients observe the WebSocket connection appear to hang (no tokens for ~10–30s) and then either reconnect or receive a 503. This happens every few minutes and seems to correlate with large bursts (10–20 concurrent sessions).

Attached is a quick timeline (atlas-client-timeline.csv) showing timestamps from three locations and the client-side reconnect traces. Example: 2028-02-22T14:03:12Z — no tokens for 18s, reconnect at 14:03:30Z.

Impact: customers see slow UX and some dropped requests. Procurement flagged this to leadership because it affects demos. Can your team prioritize? We can provide temporary API keys or replay traces if you need them.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 18:05:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: Realtime feed freeze — quick triage findings

Doing a quick pass on the runtime traces Jordan attached and the customer timeline. Initial observations:

- We see repeated stall periods where the chunked transfer window stops emitting tokens for 8–25s. The TCP connection remains established; there are no immediate FINs.
- Kernel-side: increased P50->P99 delta for attention and kv-cache refill on the quantized variant of the gpt-like model used by Atlas. The quantized path is choosing a smaller kernel that is hitting serialization points on high concurrency.
- Network keepalive: noticed that some upstream proxies are not sending application-level pings during the stall window (keepalive TTL shows gaps).

Attached: runtime-trace-logs.txt with oid markers.

Short-term plan (can implement within 2–3 hours):
1) Increase application-level WebSocket keepalive frequency (from 30s to 10s) and lower chunk flush threshold so clients see partial tokens sooner.
2) Enable transparent fallback to the non-quantized model variant for Atlas sessions during the surge window.
3) If stalls persist, spin up an isolated ded. pool for Atlas traffic to remove noisy-neighbor contention.

I need customer debug tokens or a replay bundle to reproduce locally (Jordan, can you provide?). Also going to open a JIRA (SUP-1234) and attach traces.

—Rishi
Sr. Software Engineer, Inference Runtime

Date: Sat, 25 Feb 2028 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Final triage update & remediation plan (board prep)

Team — post-call notes and proposed permanent fixes for Atlas:

Summary: intermittent 8–25s token emission stalls caused by a convergence of three factors: (1) quantized kernel serialization at high concurrency, (2) upstream proxy keepalive gaps that delay application-level pings, and (3) a chunk-flush heuristic that deferred partial-token flushes under certain tail latencies.

Remediation plan (next milestones):
- Immediate (within 24h): ship change to increase keepalive frequency and lower chunk flush threshold globally for high-concurrency sessions. This reduces visible stalls and gives the client earlier partial tokens.
- Short (48–72h): provide a selective configuration in the Console to pin Atlas to the non-quantized model variant or a dedicated pool.
- Medium (1–2 weeks): runtime kernel patch to remove the serialization hotspot on the quantized path. Patch attached: patch-keepalive-chunk-threshold.diff and linked to SUP-1234.
- Communications: Monica/Stephanie prepare a one-page exec summary for Atlas leadership and our board-facing incident blurb.

I recommend marking this P1 for the weekend runbook and tracking impact on SLAs if recurrence continues.

—Rishi
Sr. Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
